newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher, market remains rangebound.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher, market remains rangebound.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed slightly higher as the market found solid support just above recent lows, dealers said.
They noted producer sales in the cash market had dried up following last week's decline in prices. Commission houses were featured buyers.
September dipped early to a low of $3.62-1/2 a bushel, just above key support at its recent low of $3.61 (set on August 5) but recovered to end 2-3/4 cents higher at $3.67-1/4.
Other months ended 4-1/2 to one cent higher.
Dealers noted the market had been trading in a narrow range for more than three weeks.
Harvest delays in U.S. spring wheat areas were a background supportive influence along with expectations that both Pakistan and Egypt could buy U.S. wheat in the next couple of weeks.
Volume was estimated at 23.8 million bushels, compared with 31.5 million on Friday.
